row.category: Vertical SaaS (Healthcare, Education, Real Estate, Construction, Field Service)
row.evidence: NationBuilder's SSO guide (Enterprise or Network plans only) describes just-in-time creation of users who sign in through the identity provider and manual identity mappings; no SCIM endpoint is documented in the help centre or the v2 API reference.
row.notes: Status unchanged (none). Pricing is per nation and scales by contact count, not per user, so per-user fields are null; annual billing is the default toggle on the pricing page. SAML/OIDC SSO is Enterprise (or Network) only, as is developer API access. The only automated account creation is JIT on SSO sign-in (with a default control-panel permission set); deprovisioning is manual, apart from control panel users who have not logged in for a year being switched to Inactive. The v2 API manages people (signups) and exposes a read-only 'is the signup a control panel user' flag but has no endpoint for control panel users or permission sets. Okta's OIN app (2020) is SAML only.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Developer API access is Enterprise, but it has no control-panel-user management endpoints.

limitations.text: Control panel users are not deprovisioned automatically; users who have not logged in for a year are switched to Inactive.

scim.notes: false by absence: no SCIM in the help-centre sitemap, the SSO guides or the v2 OpenAPI spec; the SSO guide only offers JIT or manual identity mappings.

rate_limits.text: 250 requests per 10 seconds per IP and per API token.

limitations.text: The v2 API (Enterprise) covers people, donations, events and lists; control panel access is only visible as a signup's is_cpu flag, with no endpoints for control panel users or permission sets.

user_api.notes: available=false means no documented API for managing control panel (admin) users; the people/CRM API itself exists. Spec paths are /api/v2/...; the host is not stated consistently (nation slug vs api.nationbuilder.com), so base_url is null.

okta.notes: OIN page (last updated Sep 2020) has only SAML checked (read from page markup). NationBuilder's current SSO guide sets Okta up via OIDC.

entra.notes: NationBuilder lists Entra ID as a supported SSO provider (c15), but no Entra gallery tutorial was found (saas-apps/nationbuilder-tutorial 404).

google.notes: NationBuilder supports Google Workspace via OIDC SSO (c15); no Marketplace/provisioning app checked.
